title: SSH and file transfer
goal: Create SSH keys with the right permissions, use an SSH config file, copy files safely with rsync, and debug common SSH errors.
setup: # all keys and configs go into practice folders, NOT your real ~/.ssh
# P2: an SSH config file for the team servers

printf '%s\n' 'Host bastion' '    HostName 203.0.113.10' '    User ec2-user' '    IdentityFile ~/bash-practice/day19/dot-ssh/id_todo' '' 'Host todo-prod' '    HostName 10.0.1.10' '    User deploy' '    Port 2222' '    IdentityFile ~/bash-practice/day19/dot-ssh/id_todo' '    ServerAliveInterval 30' '' 'Host *.todo.internal' '    User deploy' '    ProxyJump bastion' > dot-ssh/config
# P4/P5: a build folder to copy
cp -r build site-build          # P5 has its own copy

printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' '# Copy the CONTENTS of site-build/ into release/ (not a site-build/ folder inside release/).' '# Never copy .env files. Show a dry run first, then copy for real.' 'rsync -av site-build release/' > deploy-copy.sh

warmup.q: Which command shows which process listens on port 8080?
What does curl exit code 7 mean? And 28?
What permission must a private key or `.env` file have?
warmup.a: 600 (only the owner can read and write).

warmup.q: Why can root still read a 600 file of another user?
warmup.a: Root ignores read and write permissions. 600 protects only from other normal users.

problems.title: Create a key pair with the right permissions
problems.situation: The user needs a new SSH key to log in to the to-do servers and for Jenkins to deploy. SSH refuses keys and folders with loose permissions, so the user creates an ed25519 key in the practice folder and sets 700 / 600 / 644.
task: Create a key with no passphrase (for practice only): `ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -C 'wicky@laptop' -f dot-ssh/id_todo`.
List the two files and show their permissions with `stat -c '%a %n'`.
Set the folder to 700, the private key to 600, the public key to 644. Show them again.
Show the start of the public key and its fingerprint type with `ssh-keygen -l`.
hints: The private key has no extension; the public key ends in `.pub`. Only the `.pub` file is ever shared.
700 = only the owner can enter the folder. 600 = only the owner can read the key.
`ssh-keygen -l -f key.pub` prints bits, fingerprint, comment and type.

explanation.meaning: Modern, short and fast key type. Use RSA 4096 only for very old servers.
Empty passphrase. Fine for practice and some automation; for a personal key, use a passphrase plus ssh-agent.
A comment, so people know whose key it is.
Folder only for the owner / private key only for the owner / public key readable.
Fingerprint: a short id of the key, to compare with what the server shows.
On a real server: adds the user's `.pub` key to the server's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`.

problems.expected_output:
config	id_todo  id_todo.pub
755 dot-ssh
600 dot-ssh/id_todo
644 dot-ssh/id_todo.pub
700 dot-ssh
600 dot-ssh/id_todo
644 dot-ssh/id_todo.pub
ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZ
256 wicky@laptop (ED25519)
problems.output_note: The real key text and fingerprint are random, so only the fixed parts are printed. On a normal machine, the default key path is `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`.
mistakes: Sending the private key (without `.pub`) to someone. Never share it; send only the `.pub` file.
Running `ssh-keygen` with the default path when `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` exists: it asks to overwrite. Answering `y` loses the old key.
Committing keys or `.env` files to git. Add them to `.gitignore`.
problems.interview_say: I create keys with `ssh-keygen -t ed25519`, share only the `.pub` file, and keep `~/.ssh` at 700 and the private key at 600, otherwise SSH refuses to use it.
problems.try_yourself: Create a second key with a passphrase: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f dot-ssh/id_pass`. Then load it with ssh-agent (Extra E1).

problems.title: ~/.ssh/config: short names for servers
problems.situation: The user types `ssh -i ~/keys/id_todo -p 2222 deploy@10.0.1.10` many times a day. An SSH config file gives each server a short name. Private servers behind a bastion (jump host) can be reached in one step with `ProxyJump`.
task: Read `dot-ssh/config`.
Show what `ssh todo-prod` would use, without connecting: `ssh -G -F dot-ssh/config todo-prod`, filtered to hostname, user, port and identityfile.
Do the same for `api.todo.internal`. Which jump host is used?
Write down the full command you no longer need to type.
hints: `-F FILE` = use this config file instead of `~/.ssh/config`. `-G` = print the final settings and exit.
`Host *.todo.internal` is a pattern: it matches every name ending in `.todo.internal`.
`grep -E '^(hostname|user|port|identityfile|proxyjump) '`

explanation.meaning: The short name the user types: `ssh todo-prod`.
Real address, login user, port and key for that name.
Send a keep-alive every 30 s so idle connections are not cut.
For every internal name, go through the bastion first (same as `ssh -J bastion host`).
Print the settings ssh would use. Great for debugging configs; it does not connect.

mistakes: Wrong permissions on `~/.ssh/config`: `Bad owner or permissions on /home/wicky/.ssh/config`. Use `chmod 600 ~/.ssh/config`.
Putting `Host *` with settings at the top: the first value found wins, so later host blocks cannot override it. Put `Host *` at the end.
problems.interview_say: I keep servers in `~/.ssh/config` with HostName, User, Port and IdentityFile, and use `ProxyJump` for private servers behind a bastion. `ssh -G host` shows what will be used.
problems.try_yourself: Add a `Host todo-staging` block with `HostName 10.0.2.10` and `User deploy`, then check it with `ssh -G`.

problems.title: Explain the error: UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE
problems.situation: A teammate copied the deploy key from Windows to WSL, and SSH says `WARNING: UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE!` and `bad permissions`. The user reproduces the error, fixes it, and also prepares the server side: `authorized_keys` with the right permissions.
task: Create a key in `dot-ssh/team_key` (like P1). Set it to 644 by mistake.
Try to read it: `ssh-keygen -y -f dot-ssh/team_key`. Read the whole error.
Fix the permission and try again (print only the key type).
Prepare the server side in `server-home`: create `.ssh/authorized_keys` with the public key, folder 700, file 600.
hints: SSH ignores private keys that other users can read: 644 is "too open".
`ssh-keygen -y -f KEY` prints the public key from a private key.
On the server: `~/.ssh` = 700, `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` = 600, and the home folder must not be writable by others.

explanation.meaning: The key is readable by group or others (0644). SSH ignores it: `Load key ...: bad permissions`.
SSH tools use 255 for their own errors.
On the server: one public key per line. A user can log in with any matching private key.
sshd (with StrictModes) refuses keys if `~/.ssh` or `authorized_keys` can be written by others.
Files under `/mnt/c/...` often show as 777. Copy keys into the Linux home (`~/.ssh`) and chmod there.

problems.expected_output:
@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
@         WARNING: UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE!          @
@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
Permissions 0644 for 'dot-ssh/team_key' are too open.
It is required that your private key files are NOT accessible by others.
This private key will be ignored.
Load key "dot-ssh/team_key": bad permissions
exit code: 255
ssh-ed25519
700 server-home/.ssh
600 server-home/.ssh/authorized_keys
ssh-ed25519 deploy@jenkins
mistakes: Fixing it with `chmod 400` on the folder: then SSH cannot read anything inside. Folder 700, key 600 (or 400).
Pasting a public key into `authorized_keys` with a line break in the middle: the key does not match. One key = one line.
problems.interview_say: SSH refuses a private key that others can read, so it must be 600. On the server, `~/.ssh` must be 700 and `authorized_keys` 600; otherwise key login fails and falls back to password or `Permission denied (publickey)`.
problems.try_yourself: Add the option `from="10.0.0.0/8"` before the key in `authorized_keys`. What does it allow and block?

problems.title: rsync -avz --dry-run (and scp)
problems.situation: The user copies the frontend build to the web server. `scp` copies everything every time; `rsync` copies only changes and can show what it would do first. Here the target is a local folder, so no server is needed; the commands are the same with `user@host:/path`.
task: Dry run: `rsync -avz --dry-run build/ web-root/`. Read the file list.
Copy for real. Then run the same command again: what is copied the second time?
Delete `build/js/app.js`, then dry run with `--delete`. What would be removed on the target?
Copy one file with `scp build/index.html backup-index.html` (scp also works locally).
hints: `-a` archive (keep times, permissions, folders), `-v` verbose, `-z` compress during transfer.
The trailing `/` on `build/` means "the contents of build". Without it, rsync creates `web-root/build/`.
`--delete` removes files on the target that are not in the source. Always dry-run it first.
solution: sleep 1                                   # so the folder time really changes

explanation.meaning: Archive: recursive, keep permissions, times, symlinks.
List files / compress data on the network.
Show what would happen, change nothing.
Copy the contents. `build` (no slash) copies the folder itself.
Nothing listed: rsync compares size and time and skips files that did not change.
Make the target an exact mirror: `deleting js/app.js`. The `js/` line means: the folder's time changed, so rsync updates it.
Hide the two summary lines (bytes, speed, speedup). They change a little on every run.

problems.expected_output:
sending incremental file list created directory web-root ./ .env index.html css/ css/app.css js/ js/app.js === second run: only changes === sending incremental file list === --delete dry run === sending incremental file list deleting js/app.js js/

Todo v2
mistakes: `rsync --delete` with the wrong target folder (for example `/var/www` instead of `/var/www/todo`): it deletes everything else there. Dry run first, always.
Mixing up the order: `rsync dest/ src/` copies in the wrong direction. The source comes first, like `cp`.
problems.interview_say: I use `rsync -avz --dry-run src/ user@host:/dest/` first, then without `--dry-run`. rsync copies only changes, and `--delete` mirrors the folder. The trailing slash on the source means "copy the contents".
problems.try_yourself: Run `rsync -avz --dry-run --exclude '*.css' build/ web-root/`. Which files are left out?

problems.title: Find the bug: the deploy-copy script
problems.situation: `deploy-copy.sh` copied the build to the server. Now the site is at `/release/site-build/index.html` instead of `/release/index.html`, and the secret `.env` file is public on the web server.
task: Run `bash deploy-copy.sh`, then `find release | sort`. Compare with the comments in the script.
Find 3 problems: the trailing slash, the missing exclude, and no dry run.
Delete `release`, fix the script, and run it. Check with `find release | sort`.
hints: `rsync -av site-build release/` copies the folder `site-build` itself into release.
`--exclude '.env'` (or `--exclude '*.env'`) keeps secrets out.
First `rsync -av --dry-run ...`, then the real command.
solution: # Copy the CONTENTS of site-build/ into release/ (not a site-build/ folder inside release/).
# Never copy .env files. Show a dry run first, then copy for real.

explanation.meaning: Bug 1: the slash after `site-build` copies the contents, not the folder.
Bug 2: secrets must never reach a web root.
Bug 3: the goal said "dry run first".
An array keeps the options the same for both runs (Day 8).
Stop if a command fails (Day 22).

problems.title: ssh-agent: type the passphrase once
problems.situation: The user's real key has a passphrase (good security), but typing it for every `git pull` and `ssh` is slow. `ssh-agent` keeps the unlocked key in memory for this session.
task: Create a practice key `dot-ssh/agent_key` (no passphrase here, for speed).
Start an agent: `eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"`. Check that `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` is set.
Add the key with `ssh-add` and list keys with `ssh-add -l`.
Stop the agent with `ssh-agent -k`.
hints: `ssh-agent -s` prints shell commands; `eval` runs them to set the variables.
`ssh-add -l` lists the loaded keys; `ssh-add -D` removes all.
`ssh -A` (agent forwarding) lets a server use the user's agent: only use it with trusted servers.

explanation.meaning: Start the agent and set `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` and `SSH_AGENT_PID` in this shell.
Unlock the key once (asks for the passphrase) and keep it in the agent.
List keys: bits, fingerprint, comment, type.
Kill this agent.

problems.expected_output:
agent is running
Identity added: dot-ssh/agent_key (wicky@laptop)
256 wicky@laptop (ED25519)
agent stopped
mistakes: `ssh-add` without a running agent: `Could not open a connection to your authentication agent.` Start it with `eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"`.

checks.run: ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -f k; env -u SSH_AUTH_SOCK ssh-add k
checks.expect: Could not open a connection to your authentication agent.

problems.interview_say: I protect my key with a passphrase and load it once per session with `ssh-agent` and `ssh-add`. I avoid agent forwarding to servers I do not trust.
problems.try_yourself: Run `ssh-add -t 3600 dot-ssh/agent_key` to keep the key for one hour only.

problems.title: SSH tunnel: reach a private database (needs a server)
problems.situation: The RDS database of the vehicle parts system is in a private subnet. Only the bastion can reach it. An SSH local tunnel (`-L`) opens a port on the laptop that forwards through the bastion to the database. This needs real servers, so it is not run in the sandbox.
task: Read the command: `ssh -N -L 5433:parts-db.internal:5432 bastion`.
In a second terminal, connect to `localhost:5433` as if the database were local: `psql -h localhost -p 5433 -U app parts`.
Check the tunnel port on the laptop with `ss -ltn 'sport = :5433'`.
Stop the tunnel with Ctrl+C.
hints: `-L LOCALPORT:TARGETHOST:TARGETPORT` — the target host is resolved by the bastion, not by the laptop.
`-N` = do not run a remote command, only forward.
`-R` is the opposite (remote forward); `-D` makes a SOCKS proxy.
solution: psql -h localhost -p 5433 -U app parts -c 'select count(*) from parts;'

explanation.meaning: Listen on laptop port 5433; send traffic through SSH to parts-db.internal:5432.
Host name from `~/.ssh/config` (P2).
Only the tunnel, no shell.
Programs on the laptop connect here.

problems.output_note: Typical output; the row count is example data. The tunnel needs a reachable bastion and database.
problems.typical_output:
State  Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address:Port Peer Address:Port Process
LISTEN 0      128        127.0.0.1:5433      0.0.0.0:*
 count
-------
  1284
(1 row)
mistakes: `bind [127.0.0.1]:5433: Address already in use`: a tunnel or local Postgres already uses 5433. Pick another local port.
Leaving tunnels open in the background after work. Stop them, or use `ssh -O exit` with ControlMaster.
problems.interview_say: To reach a private database I use an SSH local forward through a bastion: `ssh -N -L 5433:db:5432 bastion`, then connect to localhost:5433. In AWS, SSM Session Manager port forwarding is an option without open SSH ports.
problems.try_yourself: Write the `LocalForward 5433 parts-db.internal:5432` line into a `Host db-tunnel` block in `dot-ssh/config`.

problems.title: Debug SSH errors: refused, timeout, permission denied
problems.situation: "I cannot SSH to the server" can mean very different problems. The exact error shows where to look. The user creates one real error (connection refused to a closed local port) and learns the others with a table.
task: Try `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=3 -p 2222 127.0.0.1` (nothing listens on 2222). Read the error and exit code.
Check the port with `nc -zv 127.0.0.1 2222`.
Read the table: which error points to the network, the server, or the key?
hints: `BatchMode=yes` = never ask for a password, fail instead (good in scripts).
`Connection refused` = the host answered, but nothing listens on that port.
`ssh -v` (or `-vvv`) prints each step: which key is offered, what the server answers.
solution: ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=3 -p 2222 127.0.0.1 true; echo "ssh exit code: $?"

explanation.meaning: The server is reachable, but sshd is not running or listens on another port.
ssh's own error (not the remote command's exit code).
Confirms the port is closed, without SSH.

problems.expected_output:
ssh: connect to host 127.0.0.1 port 2222: Connection refused
ssh exit code: 255
nc: connect to 127.0.0.1 port 2222 (tcp) failed: Connection refused
nc exit code: 1
mistakes: Deleting `~/.ssh/known_hosts` completely after `Host key verification failed`. Remove only that host with `ssh-keygen -R host`, after confirming the change is expected.
problems.interview_say: I read the exact SSH error: refused means nothing listens, timeout means network or firewall, `Permission denied (publickey)` means key, user or permissions. Then I use `ssh -v` to see each step.
problems.try_yourself: Run `ssh -v -o BatchMode=yes -p 2222 127.0.0.1 2>&1 | head -n 5` and read the first debug lines.

interview.q: How do you set up key-based SSH login?
interview.a: Create a key with `ssh-keygen -t ed25519`, copy the public key to the server with `ssh-copy-id user@host` (it goes into `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`), then log in with the private key.

interview.q: What permissions do `~/.ssh`, the private key and `authorized_keys` need?
interview.a: `~/.ssh` 700, the private key 600, `authorized_keys` 600 (public keys 644). SSH refuses looser permissions.

interview.q: What is the difference between scp and rsync?
interview.a: scp always copies whole files. rsync copies only changes, can resume, can `--delete` to mirror, and has `--dry-run`.

interview.q: What is a bastion (jump host), and how do you use it?
interview.a: A hardened server in a public subnet used to reach private servers. `ssh -J bastion private-host`, or `ProxyJump bastion` in `~/.ssh/config`.
It opens port 5433 on my machine and forwards it through the bastion to db:5432, so I can reach a private database at localhost:5433.
